shots.purpose: Open on a long lake in frozen hills: the wrongness of the answer hiding in plain sight
shots.claim: Lake Baikal alone holds more unfrozen fresh surface water than the North American Great Lakes combined
shots.evidence: full-bleed plate: a long icy lake stretching between dark hills under cold light, no depth shown yet
shots.motion_reason: slow push-in so the long lake reads as the subject

subject_contract.expected_subject: survey plate of a long icy lake between dark hills under cold light

shots.purpose: Show the depth: a sounding line dropping far past any other lake's bottom
shots.claim: Lake Baikal is the deepest lake on Earth; its volume spread over North America would cover it by roughly a metre
shots.evidence: cross-section card: a plumb line descending through banded water to a lake floor far below, depth ticks along the way
shots.motion_reason: drift down the sounding line so the depth is the motion

subject_contract.expected_subject: survey cross-section: sounding line through banded water to a deep lake floor with depth ticks

shots.purpose: Reveal the ledger: one Baikal vessel towering over the combined Great Lakes vessel
shots.claim: Baikal holds roughly one fifth of Earth's unfrozen fresh surface water, at 1,642 metres the deepest lake
shots.evidence: split card: left, one tall full water vessel labeled Baikal; right, a shorter vessel for all five Great Lakes together
shots.motion_reason: held framing; the vessel-height contrast is the information

subject_contract.expected_subject: survey split: one tall full water vessel beside a shorter combined-lakes vessel

one_second.relationship: one vessel out-holds five great ones

surprise.evidence: the calm lake surface opens into a cross-section of the crust beneath it, pulled apart on both sides with the basin sinking

shots.purpose: Show the engine: crust pulled apart, basin sinking, water collecting in the tear
shots.claim: Baikal lies in an active continental rift that keeps widening, so the basin keeps deepening
shots.evidence: cross-section card: two crust blocks with outward arrows, a sinking graben between them, the lake filling the tear
shots.motion_reason: drift across the pull-apart so the sinking basin is the motion

subject_contract.expected_subject: survey cross-section: two crust blocks pulled apart with outward arrows and a sinking basin filled by the lake

one_second.relationship: the crust tears and the basin sinks

shots.purpose: Show what isolation builds: transparent flesh fish and sponge gardens found nowhere else
shots.claim: at roughly 25 million years Baikal is the world's oldest lake, and most of its species are endemics found nowhere else
shots.evidence: specimen card: a transparent golomyanka-style fish beside branching sponge forms on the deep floor, both drawn as survey specimens
shots.motion_reason: drift across the specimens so the strangeness is the information

subject_contract.expected_subject: survey specimen plate: transparent fish and branching sponges drawn as chart specimens

shots.purpose: Show the paradox: a seal on lake ice, with the ocean an unreachable distance away
shots.claim: the Baikal seal (nerpa) lives and breeds entirely in fresh water, far from any ocean; its route there is debated
shots.evidence: chart card: a seal resting on lake ice in the foreground, a long dashed route arc receding toward a distant ocean edge
shots.motion_reason: drift along the route arc so the impossible distance is the motion

subject_contract.expected_subject: survey chart: seal on lake ice with a long dashed route arc toward a distant ocean

one_second.relationship: a seal a thousand kilometres from home

shots.purpose: Land the argument on the same cross-section at dusk: ancient, deepening, still opening
shots.claim: Baikal is an ancient, still-active rift lake that keeps deepening as the rift opens
shots.evidence: dusk reprise: the rift cross-section in warm light, water banded deep, the tear still faintly widening
shots.motion_reason: slow pull-out, the frame settles as the argument does

subject_contract.expected_subject: survey cross-section at dusk: deep banded water in a rift valley, calm warm light

one_second.relationship: the archive is still being written
